analysis: This batch contains only documentation changes: docs/architecture/inference.md (head text at lines 1232-1777, plus a patch excerpt at about 1116-1128 adding Qwen inline-MTP ordinary-decode-history prose) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (new benchmark flags --runtime-concurrency and --runtime-stagger, lines 519 and 1145-1146). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, or cache-storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence. I checked the docs against the threat model assets and boundaries. The MTP chained-history prose describes hidden-state carry held in assistant history and does not touch the SSD prefix cache (T-041). The prefix-cache scope, HMAC naming, and TTL mitigations are not altered. The CLI flags are benchmark-only, run with the prefix cache off, and emit per-row tokens and timings as JSON. Nothing shows them reaching coordinator traffic or consumer prompts. Benchmark outputs may include generated text and tokens, but that is local operator-run benchmarking with an operator-supplied prompt, not consumer data (A-001). Unverified contracts: the actual implementation of EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark, and the new env rollback switches (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED/CARRY) are not in the supplied batch. Any source change there needs separate review, particularly on hidden-state retention across rows and requests (cf. T-028 residual GPU/memory data) and on the MTP cross-request carry. The cli-reference patch excerpt is truncated at line 519 of base, but the range map is complete. No regressions or threat-model invalidations are identified from the docs alone.
